text.p: Bulgaria's prime minister designate Ivan Kostov on Monday presented his cabinet to President Petar Stoyanov following his coalition's victory in April 19 elections.
The list, which will be presented to parliament on Wednesday, proposes Muravei Radev, former deputy chairman of parliament's economic commission, as finance minister, Kostov told reporters.
Radev, 50, an economist by training, will play a central role in implementation of reforms prescribed by the International Monetary Fund, including implementation of a fixed exchange rate regime.
"We shall aim to restore confidence in Bulgaria and fulfil the pledges in the accord signed with the IMF, including introduction of a currency board system," Kostov said.
Interim deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov retains the industry portfolio, overseeing the restructuring of the unwieldy state sector.

Nadezhda Mihailova, spokeswoman of Kostov's Union of Democratic Forces, becomes foreign minister, and interim interior minister Bogomil Bonev will continue his high-profile campaign against organised crime and corruption. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 91188, 981 4145
